fullDescription: Make the 1200 x 630 card that renders when a link is shared - the one image where text belongs in the pixels. Defaults to a free design-system HTML route with perfect text fidelity, and reserves generation for artwork: textless composite first, baked text on the best text-rendering model last. Platform specifications adapted from alonw0's web-asset-generator (MIT).
prompt:
# OG & Share Image

Make the `1200 × 630` card that renders when a link to the site is shared. This is the one image deliverable where the rule inverts: everywhere else, text baked into pixels is a defect - here it is the point. A share preview is a static file; no HTML arrives with it, so the headline must live in the image, at perfect fidelity, or the first impression of the product is a garbled one. That inversion decides the workflow: the route that produces flawless text costs nothing, and the routes that cost credits exist only for artwork.

## When to use

- The user asks for an OG image, share image, Twitter/X card, link preview, or social card for a site or launch post.
- A project is shipping and has no `og:image`, so shared links render as bare text.
- A launch post needs a branded card with the announcement headline on it.

Do not use for: an in-page hero or section background (use `Image Generation / Hero Visual` - that text stays in the DOM), the logo mark itself (use `Image Generation / IP as Logo`), or an ad creative sized for a paid placement.

## The canvas

- Generate at `1200 × 630` (1.91:1). Facebook, LinkedIn, and WhatsApp use it directly, and X renders it correctly as a large summary card.
- Keep every critical element - headline, logo, focal object - inside the middle `80%` of the frame. Platforms crop and overlay differently, and the outer band is where content dies.
- Headline type at this canvas size means `80px` or larger, two to three lines maximum, roughly 40 characters per line. The preview is often seen at a third of its real size in a feed; if it is not readable there, it is not readable.
- Keep the file under `1MB` - PNG for flat graphics and text, JPEG for photographic art.

## Route A - build it from the design system (free, default)

The project already contains everything a share card needs: the brand colors as tokens, the display font, the logo asset, real copy. Compose a `1200 × 630` card as HTML inside the project - a full-bleed brand-colored frame, the headline set in the actual display font, the mark placed deliberately - render it at exactly that size, and screenshot it. The text is set by a font renderer, not sampled by a diffusion model, so it is crisp at any zoom, and when the headline changes next month the card regenerates in seconds for free.

Propose this route first, every time. Only leave it when the card genuinely needs artwork the design system cannot produce - an illustration, a dimensional scene, a rendered object.

Composition rules for the card: one headline, one mark, at most one supporting visual element. Generous margins on all four sides. Title text against its background must pass `4.5:1` contrast - check it, don't eyeball it.

## Route B - generated artwork (credits)

Two sub-paths, in order of preference. State the credit cost and get agreement before generating either.

**B1 - textless art underneath, HTML text on top.** Generate a background with the full `Image Generation / Hero Visual` discipline: a quiet, tonally flat region reserved where the headline will sit, no letterforms anywhere, no words from the copy in the prompt. Then feed it into Route A as the card's background layer and set the headline in HTML. This keeps the robust text path and adds the artwork. Models: Seedream 5 Lite at `6` credits (free tier) for atmospheric art, or Nano Banana 2 at `10` credits when the art must incorporate the actual product shot or logo as a reference image (it accepts up to 10).

**B2 - text baked into the image.** The last resort, for when compositing is impossible - the card is being made for a context with no HTML step. Use Nano Banana Pro at `20` credits; its text rendering is the strongest available. GPT Image 2 also renders text well but only outputs `1:1`, `3:2`, and `2:3` - it cannot produce a 1.91:1 frame, so it is out unless you plan a deliberate crop. Wrap the exact display string in quotes in the prompt, demand crisp legible type, and inspect the result character by character at full size afterward. One wrong glyph is a rejection, not a blemish.

**The aspect-ratio trap.** `1.91:1` is not a native generation ratio. Generate at `16:9` (which yields `1200 × 675`) and crop `45px` of height. Compose for that crop from the start: nothing meaningful in the top or bottom `4%` of the generated frame, on top of the middle-80% safe zone.

## Prompt skeletons

B1, textless background:

```text
Create one 16:9 background artwork for a <product category> announcement card. This is a background only; all text is added separately in HTML.
Subject: <one sentence - the single object or the character of the abstract field>.
Composition: keep the <left half | lower two thirds> visually quiet, flat, and low-detail with no focal element in it; place visual weight in the <opposite region>. Keep all meaningful content away from the outer 10% of the frame.
Color: build from <brand color> as the <dominant field | single accent> with <supporting neutral>.
Constraints: Add no text, letters, numbers, watermarks, or logos. No frames, borders, cards, or device bezels. Keep the quiet region free of high-contrast detail and bright highlights.
```

B2, baked text (Nano Banana Pro):

```text
Create one 16:9 social share card for <product category>.
Headline: render the exact text "<display string>" in <2|3> lines of large, crisp, perfectly legible <sans-serif | serif> type, no garbled or invented characters, centered in the <left 60% | middle> of the frame.
Backdrop: <flat brand-colored field | described artwork>, holding the area behind the headline tonally flat and <dark | light> for contrast.
Composition: keep the headline and every meaningful element inside the middle 80%; nothing within the top or bottom 4%.
Constraints: Render only the quoted headline - no other text, labels, numbers, watermarks, or logos. No frames, borders, or UI elements.
```

## Favicon and app icons - the mark, not the card

The companion assets are downscaled versions of the *mark*, never of the OG card. If the project lacks a usable mark, create one with `Image Generation / IP as Logo` first - its 32 × 32 readability requirement is exactly the favicon requirement. Then produce the set from that one square artwork: `32` and `16` for browser tabs, `180` apple-touch, `192` and `512` for PWA manifests. App-icon sizes need a solid background (iOS rounds the corners itself; transparency turns black on some launchers), and the tab sizes should be checked against both a light and a dark browser chrome.

## Delivering it

The card is inert until the page points at it:

```html
<meta property="og:image" content="https://<site>/og-image.png" />
<meta property="og:image:width" content="1200" />
<meta property="og:image:height" content="630" />
<meta property="og:image:alt" content="<what the card shows>" />
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
```

The URL must be absolute and HTTPS - platforms fetch it server-side, so `localhost` and relative paths silently produce empty previews. Platforms also cache aggressively: after replacing a card, the old one keeps appearing until the platform's sharing debugger is told to re-scrape. Say this to the user; it is the most common "it didn't work" report.

## Reject a candidate when

- Any generated character is malformed, invented, doubled, or subtly wrong - read every glyph at 100% zoom. This kills more B2 candidates than everything else combined.
- The headline or logo strays outside the middle 80%, or meaningful content sits in the top or bottom 4% that the 16:9 → 1.91:1 crop removes.
- Title text fails `4.5:1` contrast against the pixels it actually sits on.
- The card is illegible at one-third scale - squint-test it at ~400px wide, the size a feed actually shows.
- Extra text, watermarks, or pseudo-letterforms appear anywhere outside the intended headline.
- The art introduces a color outside the project's palette, or the card reads as a generic gradient-with-slogan template.
- The frame is stretched or letterboxed instead of composed for 1.91:1.

Always view the finished card at both full size and feed size, with the real headline, before shipping it - and prefer having never left Route A at all.

---

Platform specifications adapted from [web-asset-generator](https://github.com/alonw0/web-asset-generator) by @alonw0, MIT licensed.

Rewritten for Superdesign: the Python asset pipeline replaced with a design-system-first HTML route rendered from the project's own tokens, generation demoted to an artwork-only fallback with a textless-composite path and a baked-text path on the best text-rendering models, the 16:9 → 1.91:1 crop discipline made explicit, and credit costs stated before any generation.
